name: At Most One Uncounted Vertex Separates Disjoint Shore Directions
statement: Suppose the active slice is $L=\{a\}$, the nonempty passive shores are pairwise disjoint, and the uncounted remainder satisfies $\eta\le1$. If distinct shores $S_z,S_w$ contain active edges of directions $f_z,f_w$, then $f_z\ne f_w$. Consequently the active--passive pairs $\{z,f_z\}$ and $\{w,f_w\}$ are disjoint.
proof: If both shore edges had direction $f$, their passive flips would be two $f$-edges of $K$ in the one-coordinate layers $\sigma\oplus z$ and $\sigma\oplus w$. Their anchor family is ample and connected. At the first anchor-path step that changes the passive restriction, the new edge lies either in the base layer, which contains only the singleton lift and no edge, or in a layer with at least two passive flips. Pairwise shore disjointness puts all forced fibres and collars in one-coordinate layers, so both endpoints in the latter layer would be uncounted, forcing $\eta\ge2$. Both possibilities contradict the assumptions.
